comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
INVESTIGATION (Phase 1, analysis only — no code changed; operator-directed 2026-08-04 re-check of the "one LLM call per pass" claim). Verdict on the prior claim, the confirmed mechanism with citations, and a remedy recommendation. DO-NOT-IMPLEMENT scope respected.

## (a) Verdict on the prior claim ("each review pass only makes ONE LLM call, so within-run caching can never hit")

ACCURATE for the measured shape, but INCOMPLETE as a general mechanism — and it is not, by itself, the root cause.

- Accurate: in the two measured runs every pass is a single single-turn call (all five usage rows show requests=1; this ticket's own table). Code confirms the leaf-review shape: the finder chunks are `execution_mode="single_turn"` unless the code-grounding tier (passes.py:319, pass1_chunk), the ISF/verifier/prereq-verifier/coach templates all declare `execution_mode: single_turn`, and a leaf ticket whose LLM-tier criteria fit ONE facet chunk yields exactly one plan-reviewer call (`registry.chunk_by_facet`, pass1.py:447). Five passes, five calls, five DISTINCT system prompts.
- Incomplete: rebar's caching design was never premised on multi-call-per-pass alone. Within-run reuse is real and measured where >1 call shares a prefix: Pass-1 warm-then-fan-out (pass1.py:519-527, story 25fa) and the container warm-then-fan-out (pass1.py:237-267; story 0250 de-risk A measured 1 write / 8 reads across an epic fan-out), plus intra-call agentic reuse (this ticket: cache_read=386204 / 493547 on multi-step code reviews). So "the cache is categorically wasted" is wrong; it is wasted on the SINGLE-CHUNK LEAF review shape — which the measured runs happened to be, and which is the common case.

## (b) Root cause of zero cache reads — three distinct mechanisms, with citations

1. WITHIN one run, cross-pass reads are structurally impossible with the current marker placement. `cache_settings_for` (capabilities.py:611; settings at 649-668) sets only the instructions + tool-definitions breakpoints on single_turn calls, i.e. ONE breakpoint at the END of the whole system prompt. The three plan-bearing passes deliberately share a byte-identical LEADING segment — `shared_plan_prefix(plan)` (prompts.py:398-407: stance preamble + whole plan) is prepended for the finder (passes.py:290) and embedded as the verifier template's leading `{{shared_prefix}}` (plan_review_verifier.md:11) — but provider prompt caching keys entries on the EXACT bytes up to the breakpoint, and each pass's breakpoint sits after its pass-specific stance suffix. Three different suffixes → three different cache keys → 3 writes, 0 reads, every run. The byte-identity engineering of story 9374 is real but unexploitable: no breakpoint exists at the shared-prefix boundary. (The prereq-verifier is worse: its template puts its stance FIRST and `{{plan}}` at line 16, so even its leading bytes differ.)

2. ACROSS runs on DIFFERENT tickets, reads are impossible BY DESIGN, not by accident. The marked prefix embeds the whole plan (that is the point — it is the stable bytes re-sent across a run's fan-out). Content-addressed caching cannot reuse a plan-bearing prefix across different plans. The measured experiment (1c39 then 9baf — two different tickets) therefore GUARANTEED zero reads regardless of any defect. This is the key correction to this ticket's framing: the prefix does not "vary per ticket" through instability — it varies because the plan is IN it, deliberately (stories 0250/8415/9374/25fa all build on that placement).

3. ACROSS runs on the SAME ticket within the ~5-min TTL, the prefix IS byte-stable and WOULD read: plan_text is exactly title+description (det_floor.py:164-166), the templates are static files, and no timestamp/ordering-unstable content enters `_resolve_system` (passes.py:269-291 — variables are only {plan, shared_prefix}). The gate sequence just rarely re-reviews the same unchanged ticket within 5 minutes, so this path almost never fires in practice. (This ticket's dd27 sibling even recorded an ACCIDENTAL same-prefix cross-run hit inside the TTL during measurement — confirming mechanism 3 works.)

Corollary: this ticket's AC "the marked prefix for a given pass is byte-identical across TICKETS" is unsatisfiable without evicting the plan from the marked prefix — which would destroy the within-run container/chunk reuse that warm-then-fan-out is built on, and bug f81d (closed wont-fix) already DISPROVED the move-the-plan-to-the-user-message alternative at mechanism level (both `*_cache_messages` and automatic caching mark the LAST message block, which ends with per-call-unique bytes). That AC should be re-scoped.

Also confirmed as stated in the description: the coach and ticket-digest passes write 0 because their marked prefixes (~150 / ~477 tok) sit below the model floor (bug f81d, evidence unchanged: plan_review_coach.md:20 puts `<!--volatile-->` two lines from the end; enrich's payload is per-ticket user text with no reusable prefix). And the diagnostic gap is real: `warn_if_cache_ineffective` fires only on read==0 AND write==0 (structured_run.py:452-455), so the write-every-call-never-read shape is invisible to telemetry — AC 4 of this ticket stands.

## (c) Recommended remedy (NOT implemented)

ESCALATE-worthy part flagged below; the telemetry part is safe.

1. SAFE / behavior-preserving: extend `warn_if_cache_ineffective` (or a small aggregate check over the run's usage records) to flag the "wrote >0 on every call of a run, read 0 everywhere" shape. Pure observability; keeps this class loud. (This ticket's AC 4.)

2. THE REAL PRIZE — needs design + operator sign-off: place a SECOND cache breakpoint at the END of the shared plan-bearing prefix, so within one run the finder's write is READ by the Pass-2 verifier (and any other pass whose system starts with `shared_plan_prefix(plan)`), and a same-ticket re-review inside the TTL reads too. Mechanics to resolve: pydantic-ai's `anthropic_cache_instructions`/`bedrock_cache_instructions` mark only the LAST system block and `system_prompt` is a single string, so this needs either multi-block system assembly or an upstream knob — a runner-seam design change. It also wants the prereq-verifier template reordered to lead with `{{shared_prefix}}` (today its stance precedes `{{plan}}`, prerequisite_verifier.md:16), which REORDERS model-visible prompt bytes — not strictly behavior-preserving, so it needs a fidelity check and sign-off.

3. Do NOT pursue cross-ticket prefix identity (the current AC 2 as written) and do NOT disable caching on single-call passes — the former conflicts with the within-run design and f81d's disproof; the latter is explicitly warned against in this description and would forfeit the container/agentic reads that demonstrably work.

Cost impact (rough, from this ticket's own figures): a leaf review currently pays ~9.2-9.5k cache-WRITE tokens (1.25x premium) for zero reads → ~2.3k token-equivalents of pure write-premium waste per review. With a shared-prefix breakpoint, a typical plan-bearing prefix (~2-3k tok) is written once and read (0.1x) by ~2 subsequent passes: saves roughly 0.9 × 2.5k × 2 ≈ 4.5k input-token-equivalents plus ~1.2k of avoided duplicate write premium — order 5-6k token-equivalents per plan review, and more on container reviews and TTL re-reviews. Exact numbers should come from the two-ticket prefix-render diff + live A/B this ticket's Testing section already prescribes.

PHASE 2 (execution — continuation of the crashed session; ticket held in_progress by this host bot, claimed_session=null). Operator-approved scope: Remedy 1 (telemetry) + Remedy 2 (shared-prefix cache breakpoint). Not pursuing cross-ticket prefix identity or disabling caching on single-step passes.

RE-SCOPE of AC 2 ("the marked prefix for a given pass is byte-identical across TICKETS, pinned by a test verified RED"): WITHDRAWN as unsatisfiable, per this ticket's own Phase-1 investigation (b).2 and (c).3. The marked prefix embeds the whole plan BY DESIGN (shared_plan_prefix = stance preamble + full plan; stories 0250/8415/9374/25fa build on that placement); content-addressed caching therefore cannot reuse a plan-bearing prefix across DIFFERENT plans, and bug f81d (wont-fix) already disproved the move-plan-to-user-message alternative at the mechanism level. Cross-ticket identity would require evicting the plan from the marked prefix, which destroys the within-run container/chunk reuse warm-then-fan-out depends on.

AC 2 is REPLACED by an in-session-achievable AC: the marked cache breakpoint lands at the END of the byte-identical shared_plan_prefix boundary (not after the pass-specific stance suffix), pinned by an OFFLINE unit test against real pydantic-ai _map_message for BOTH the anthropic and bedrock cache styles, so within one run the finder cache WRITE is READ by the Pass-2 verifier and a same-ticket re-review inside the TTL reads too.

Mechanism (verified offline): pydantic-ai's anthropic_cache_instructions / bedrock_cache_instructions place the system cache_control on the LAST STATIC block; a DYNAMIC instruction after a static system block moves the breakpoint to the end of that static block. So: pass shared_plan_prefix as the system_prompt (static) and the pass-specific stance suffix as a DYNAMIC instruction — the model still receives prefix+suffix byte-identically (behaviour-preserving; only the cache boundary moves). Delivered via a new RunRequest.cache_prefix runner-seam knob assembled in agent_call.build_agent_kwargs; wired into the Pass-1 finder (writes) and the Pass-2 verifier workflow step (reads), plus the prerequisite_verifier template reordered to LEAD with {{shared_prefix}} (fidelity-checked). Remedy 1: warn_if_cache_ineffective gains a write>0/read==0 aggregate detector. Live A/B minimised per operator direction; hit proven via the offline breakpoint-boundary test + render diff.

PHASE 2 COMPLETE (implementation landed for review; ticket left in_progress pending CI). Both operator-approved remedies are implemented, tested OFFLINE, and pushed to Gerrit.

GERRIT CHANGE: 1386 — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1386
Local commit: 777e885cb6 ("1dbe: read prompt cache across plan-review passes"), rebar-ticket trailer present, DCO-signed, Change-Id Id60c2a5.

WHAT LANDED:
- Remedy 2 (the prize): new RunRequest.cache_prefix runner-seam knob. When set to a byte-stable proper prefix of system_prompt, agent_call.build_agent_kwargs sends the prefix as the static system_prompt and the REMAINDER as a zero-arg DYNAMIC instruction — pydantic-ai's anthropic/bedrock cache-instructions then place the breakpoint at the PREFIX boundary (they mark the last STATIC block). Model still receives prefix+remainder byte-identically; only the cache boundary moves. Wired into the Pass-1 finder (passes.py, cache_prefix=shared_plan_prefix(plan)) so it WRITES at the shared boundary, and into every verify step via workflow/runs.build_agent_request (reads ctx.inputs["shared_prefix"]) so the Pass-2 verifiers READ that write within one run. Prerequisite-verifier template reordered to LEAD with {{shared_prefix}} (dropped its trailing {{plan}} block, whose bytes the prefix already carries); prerequisite_workflow_ops + its output schema + plan-review.yaml pass shared_prefix through.
- Remedy 1 (AC4 telemetry): structured_run.cache_write_never_read + warn_if_cache_write_never_read detect the write-every-call/read-0 run shape; usage_log.summarize calls it over the run's rows. The per-call warn_if_cache_ineffective (write==0 AND read==0) could never see this shape.

TESTS (offline, no live LLM):
- NEW tests/unit/test_cache_prefix_breakpoint.py (10): breakpoint-boundary proof against REAL pydantic-ai _map_message (anthropic) / _map_messages (bedrock) — cache_control/cachePoint lands exactly on the shared prefix block; plus the write>0/read==0 telemetry detector/warn and no-op guards (no cache_prefix, non-proper-prefix ignored).
- tests/unit/workflow/test_shared_prefix.py +3: prereq-verifier now LEADS with shared_plan_prefix, no stance/plan content lost by the reorder (fidelity check), and verify-inputs emits shared_prefix.
- Updated test_plan_review_prerequisites_heldout for the new shared_prefix output key.
- Regression: full llm/plan_review/prerequisite/cache/prompt/usage/runner sweep green (1445 passed). The only failures in the tree are pre-existing test_web_tool_gating cases that ImportError on the missing ddgs/duckduckgo_search dep — identical on origin/main, unrelated to this change.

GATES: make lint clean; make typecheck clean (mypy, 430 files); module-size cap respected — passes.py at exactly 800/800 (consolidated three function-local `from ...prompting import prompts` imports to one module-level import to make room for the finder cache_prefix line). Live A/B skipped per operator direction: the hit is proven by the offline breakpoint-boundary test + the byte-identical-prefix render alignment.

AC RE-SCOPE: the "byte-identical marked prefix across TICKETS" AC remains WITHDRAWN as unsatisfiable (see the Phase-2 comment above and investigation (b).2/(c).3), replaced by the achievable breakpoint-at-shared-prefix-boundary AC, which the offline tests pin.

CLOSE DECISION: LEFT IN_PROGRESS. Per AGENTS.md the change must reach Verified +1 (green CI) AND LLM-Review +1 before Submit, and a ticket is not closed until its change is Verified +1 — a passing completion-verifier is not a substitute for green CI. Change 1386 was just pushed and has neither vote yet, so closing now would force past a not-yet-green gate. Will close after 1386 merges (Verified +1 + LLM-Review +1 + Submit).

compiled_state.description:
# Prompt caching writes on every gate call and is never read across calls: the marked prefix is not stable

## Observed — measured, with a control

Two `rebar review-plan` runs executed BACK TO BACK, seconds apart, well inside the ~5-minute
cache TTL, on two DIFFERENT tickets (1c39 then 9baf), with REBAR_USAGE_LOG capturing every call.
All calls on Bedrock via the project default. Per-call figures:

    pass                                RUN A in / write        RUN B in / write        RUN B read
    plan-reviewer (frontier/opus)        5286 / 2800             5394 / 2908             0
    plan-review-prerequisite-verifier    3809 / 1545             3872 / 1608             0
    plan-review-verifier                 7136 / 4871             7199 / 4934             0
    plan-review-coach                    1999 / 0                2062 / 0                0
    ticket-digest (trivial/haiku)        2131 / 0                2816 / 0                0
    TOTALS                               write 9216, read 0      write 9450, read 0

RUN B WROTE THE CACHE AGAIN INSTEAD OF READING IT. Every read is zero in both runs.

## The mechanism this points at

Each pass's cache-WRITE size tracks its input size almost exactly across the two runs
(plan-reviewer 5286 -> 5394 input, 2800 -> 2908 write; verifier 7136 -> 7199 input,
4871 -> 4934 write). A cache prefix that were genuinely stable would produce the SAME marked
prefix and therefore a hit on the second run. That the write grows in step with per-ticket input
says the MARKED PREFIX ITSELF VARIES PER CALL — i.e. per-ticket content is landing ahead of the
cache breakpoint, so the cache key is unique every time and can never be reused.

`capabilities.cache_settings_for` marks the INSTRUCTIONS plus tool definitions, and
`structured_run.estimate_marked_prefix_tokens` derives the marked size from the SYSTEM PROMPT. So
the hypothesis to test first is that the rendered system prompt/instructions embed per-ticket
material (the plan text, the ticket digest, or similar) rather than being invariant across runs.

## What is NOT the explanation — ruled out by evidence

* NOT "caching is off on Bedrock". Three of five passes write thousands of tokens per run, so the
  settings are emitted and the provider accepts them.
* NOT "the read path is broken". Intra-CALL reuse demonstrably works: the production review bot's
  multi-step agentic records read large caches within a single call — e.g. a code-review pass with
  steps=9/125 logged cache_read=386204 against in=430479, and another with steps=17/125 logged
  cache_read=493547. Those are steps 2..N reusing what step 1 wrote inside one conversation.
* NOT the sub-minimum-prefix condition for the three writing passes. That condition explains the
  two passes that write ZERO — coach (whole prompt small) and ticket-digest, where the diagnostic
  fired verbatim: "only 477 tokens sit ahead of the cache breakpoint, below this model's
  4096-token minimum, while 8634 of the 9111 billed input tokens ride AFTER it unmarked". It does
  not explain a pass that writes 4871 tokens and then never reads them.

## Why it costs money rather than being merely untidy

A cache write is billed at a PREMIUM over ordinary input; a read is billed at a steep discount.
The current behaviour pays the premium on every gate call and collects the discount only within a
single multi-step call. For single-step passes — which is every pass in a plan review, all five
records show requests=1 — the write is pure loss: nothing ever reads it. Every plan review on this
project pays roughly 9,000-11,000 premium-rate cache-write tokens for zero benefit.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` `cache_settings_for` — where the breakpoints are placed.
- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` `estimate_marked_prefix_tokens` and the ineffective-cache
  diagnostic — the estimate is the instrument that would have caught this and did not.
- whatever renders the plan-review system prompt / instructions, if that is where per-ticket
  content is crossing the breakpoint.

## Approach — investigate before changing anything

The first task is NOT a fix, it is to identify precisely which bytes sit ahead of the breakpoint
and whether they vary per run. Capture the rendered system prompt for the same pass on two
different tickets and diff them; the varying region is the defect's location. Only then decide
whether the fix is to move per-ticket content behind the breakpoint (into the user message) or to
split the instructions into an invariant prefix and a per-run suffix.

Do NOT "fix" this by disabling caching on single-step passes: that trades a real, measurable
premium for giving up the cross-call discount entirely, and the cross-call discount is the larger
prize once the prefix is stable. Note also that the existing diagnostic's advice — "the changeable
thing is where the breakpoint sits, not the size of the prompt" — is exactly right here and was
never triggered for the writing passes, so consider whether the predicate should also flag
"wrote every call, never read".

## Testing

- an oracle that renders the same pass's marked prefix for two different tickets and asserts they
  are BYTE-IDENTICAL. This is the RED test: it should fail today. Verify RED before any fix.
- a live two-run oracle (the experiment above) asserting cache_read > 0 on the second run for at
  least the frontier pass, run inside the TTL.
- a guard that the ineffective-cache diagnostic fires when a pass writes on every call and never
  reads, so this class cannot recur silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the bytes that vary ahead of the cache breakpoint are identified and cited, with a diff of
      the rendered marked prefix for one pass across two different tickets.
- [ ] the marked prefix for a given pass is byte-identical across tickets, pinned by a test
      verified RED against today's behaviour.
- [ ] a second run of the same pass inside the cache TTL records cache_read > 0, evidenced by an
      actual usage-log capture rather than by inspection.
- [ ] the diagnostic in `structured_run` also flags the write-every-call-never-read shape, so a
      regression is loud.
- [ ] the cost change is stated with figures — premium-rate write tokens per review before and
      after — so the benefit is measured rather than asserted.
compiled_state.title: Prompt cache is written on every call and never read across calls: the marked prefix varies per ticket
